sights.n: Uegusuku Castle Ruins, Kume Island (宇江城城跡)
sights.w: Gusuku ruins on the 310 m summit of Uegusuku-dake — the highest castle site in Okinawa Prefecture — with a 360-degree view over almost the whole of Kume Island. Free. Designated a National Historic Site in 2009.

sights.n: Hiyajō Banta viewpoint, Kume Island (比屋定バンタ)
sights.w: Lookout on the edge of a 200 m sea cliff on Kume's north coast, looking out to the Hate-no-hama sandbar and, on clear days, the Kerama Islands. Free.

sights.n: Mīfugā rock, Kume Island (ミーフガー)
sights.w: Strange split sea-rock on Kume's north-west shore known as the 'female rock'; by local legend, childless women who pray here are blessed with children.

sights.n: Toguchi-no-hama Beach, Irabu Island (渡口の浜)
sights.w: An 800 m gently curving arc of fine white sand on south-west Irabu, renowned across Okinawa for its powdery sand and clear water, looking across to Miyako and Kurima islands; counted among Irabu's finest beaches.

sights.n: Takanazaki & Japan's Southernmost Point Monument, Hateruma (高那崎・日本最南端の碑)
sights.address: Hateruma Island, Taketomi, Yaeyama, Okinawa (south tip; ~10 min by car from Hateruma port)
sights.w: Kilometre-long limestone cliffs at the southern tip of Hateruma, Japan's southernmost inhabited island, where a monument to the southernmost point (erected 1970) stands beside Taketomi Town's peace monument and a path of stones from every prefecture.
